new_finding.title: rmcp 3.2.0 silently drops JSON-RPC batches instead of rejecting them
new_finding.severity: intermittent test-stage failure; no product data loss observed
evidence: Against the real binary on protocol 2024-11-05, after initialize + tools/list, a batch either gets -32600 Invalid request in 0.00 s or no response at all, measured by waiting 40 s. Reproduced 4 of 6 times on an idle machine.
The server stays healthy: it answers the next ordinary tools/list normally and exits 0 on stdin EOF.

The string -32600 / 'Invalid request' appears nowhere in this repository; it comes from rmcp-3.2.0/src/transport/async_rw.rs:182, which answers invalid_request only when serde classifies the parse error as Category::Data or Io, and silently ignores it for Category::Syntax or Eof.

Cargo.lock, Cargo.toml, vendor/ and crates/mcp-server/src/main.rs are byte-identical between e2ec7da and the tip; the rmcp = '=3.2.0' pin is unchanged and none of the eight commits touches the transport or the decoder.
e2ec7da built in a separate worktree reproduced at the same rate as the tip.
new_finding.recommendation: Fixing it is a transport change on already-qualified execution paths, so it belongs to its own cut with its own gate run. Until then the test stage can fail intermittently in CI and locally, and a green test stage does not prove the defect absent -- only that it did not fire in that run.

rust_hard_coded_cryptographic_value.reason: The rule fires on literals reaching a parameter named 'nonce'. In this product 'nonce' is the value of the Docker ownership label org.rust-mcp.rust-job, which proves a container or volume belongs to this process. It is not a cryptographic nonce and no cryptographic primitive is on the flagged path.
rust_hard_coded_cryptographic_value.scope_correction: The package brief describes all 31 as test literals. 21 are inside #[cfg(test)]; the other 10 are in production fingerprint helpers where the literal is the explicit sentinel "<nonce>" used to build a deterministic configuration template. The conclusion is unchanged, the scope is not.

rust_cleartext_logging.reason: The flagged 'logging' are assert_eq! failure messages inside lock_identity_accepts_only_guest_values_and_redacts_host_shapes, the test that proves host-shaped identities are redacted. They only materialize if the assertion fails.
rust_cleartext_logging.action_taken: The personal username used as a test vector was replaced with the neutral host-shaped value 'host-user'.

recommendation_to_owner: Dismiss the 31 hard-coded-cryptographic-value alerts as false positives in the Security tab, citing the assessment in M3-07.md.

Schedule renaming the ownership label away from the word 'nonce' in a later maintenance cut, not this one: the rename touches rust_applied.rs, mutation_gateway.rs, rust_gateway.rs, resolution_gateway.rs and coverage_gateway.rs, which are qualified execution paths, so it needs its own cut with its own gate run.

second_finding.action_taken: None. Fixing on an unconfirmed hypothesis would have changed qualified bytes without grounds. The oracle is correct as written.

admin_bypass.not_a_skipped_check: All five required status checks were green on the merged tip before the merge. What could not be satisfied was the review requirement, not a check.
admin_bypass.why_unsatisfiable: main requires required_approving_review_count 1 with require_code_owner_reviews true, and .github/CODEOWNERS designates @cburgosro9303 as code owner of the repository. That account authored PR #14 and is the only collaborator, and GitHub does not permit a pull request author to approve their own pull request, so the required approval could not exist.
admin_bypass.mechanism: enforce_admins was false on main, so an administrator merge was the only available path.
admin_bypass.residue: reviewDecision stays permanently recorded as REVIEW_REQUIRED on the merged PR, which is the exact fingerprint of this situation.
admin_bypass.structural_consequence: Any future milestone using the same PR flow hits this again: either add a second reviewer or expect the bypass.
